summary: Kazuhiro Yamamoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Silpakorn University, where he was supervised for his doctorate by Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya (attested 2009).
Kazuma Teshima works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He has served as a professor at Rissho University (attested in 2015 and 2026).

Kazunobu Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani University under Shiro Matsumoto. He was a lecturer at Otani University (1985–1989) and served as a professor at Bukkyo University (attested 1995–2009, 2022–2024).

Kazuo Hyodo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1972–1976) and completed his PhD at Otani University (~1978–2007) under Hajime Sakurabe, later serving as an associate professor at Otani University (~1984–2014).

Kazuo Kano works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University under Katsumi Mimaki and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg. He held posts at Koyasan University (2009–2017) and Komazawa University (from ~2017).

Kazuo Okabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He held teaching posts at Aichi Gakuin University (1969) and Komazawa University, serving as professor there from 1979 to 2006.

Kazuo Osumi is a scholar of Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1964). He served as an associate professor at Hokkaido University (1964) and professor at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977–2001).
Kazuo Oyamada specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tamagawa University and held a post at Rissho University.

Kazutoshi Ueda was a linguist and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Basil Hall Chamberlain and under Georg von der Gabelentz. He held long-term posts at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1926) and Kokugakuin University (~1918–1937).

Kazuyoshi Hotta specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies and held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2007), and later served as a term-limited assistant professor at Otani University (attested 2015).

Kazuyoshi Kino was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (1942–1948). He later served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989) and vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993).
Kazuyoshi Soma is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Meiji Yamada. He held a post as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).
Keenan W. Cox specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2014).

Kees W. Bolle was a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Leiden, Madras, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He lectured at Brown University (~1960–1964) and was a professor of history at UCLA (~1969–1994).

Kei Kataoka is an Indologist and philosopher who completed his PhD at the University of Tokyo under Hiroshi Marui and studied at the National Sanskrit University. He held posts at the University of Tokyo and has been a professor at Kyushu University.
Kei Okusa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctoral degree in literature from Otani University and serves on the faculty there (attested 2026).

Keiichi Miyamoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara. He spent his career at Kokugakuin University, serving as lecturer (1986), associate professor (1988), and professor (from 1995).
Keiji Iwata was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1944–1947). He later held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1973–1980) and Otani University.

Keiji Nishitani was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied under Kitaro Nishida and Hajime Tanabe at Kyoto University and under Martin Heidegger at Freiburg, later serving as professor at Kyoto University (1943–1964) after lecturing at Otani University.

Keiki Nakayama specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After studying and holding a post at Kyoto University (attested 2019–2020), he became a visiting scholar at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).
